findings.text: a document-backed reading is reported through the picker's 'ledger' source vocabulary and, when stale, through the detail string 'recorded account-window reading is stale', so a published Codex window can be named as a recorded ledger one. The figures are correct - the parity test asserts burn_multiple, pace_allowance and utilisation_pct - but the provenance label misnames where the reading came from. The node disclosed this limitation under follow_ons and noted the fix needs lane_context.py outside its write scope, so it does not hold the node.

justifications.durability: every added assertion has a named condition under which it reddens, and the negative control confirms the central one is load-bearing. test_paid_lanes_codex_window.py writes three rollouts (main home 39%, run home 42% at minus two minutes, a future-dated 80%) and asserts the publisher selects exactly the 42% reading, so a scanner that read only the main home, or that let a future stamp win, or that ignored the run homes, would fail; test_rollout_scan_excludes_old_readings asserts an eight-day-old reading yields no source, so removing the age bound fails it. test_dispatch_uses_published_window_as_direct_pick_does computes the direct pick BEFORE writing the document, so the two sides draw from genuinely different inputs (a recorded receipt versus the published document) rather than from one variable, and the parity on burn_multiple, pace_allowance and utilisation_pct fails if the document read is removed - shown by negative-control.log. test_dispatch_marks_old_published_window_stale reddens if the age is not carried. None of the assertions compares a value against the same variable the test passed in.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run's own gate logs are literal and complete: base-gate.log names revision=792afcbba and reports 272 passed EXIT=0; final-head-gate.log names revision=c0ec09d15 and reports 276 passed EXIT=0; head-gate.log names revision=8bd05178a and reports 276 passed EXIT=0. Neither arm reports a FAILED or ERROR line, so the added-failure set difference is empty. negative-control.log reproduces EXIT=1 by mutating the dispatch path back to recorded readings, failing exactly test_dispatch_uses_published_window_as_direct_pick_does. I independently reproduced the head arm: the two changed test files run 7 passed EXIT=0 at head 620ed51 (reviewer-logs/reviewer-head-arm.log). Weakness keeping this below the top: the shared-state production CLI pick could not be exercised because the worker fence refused the recovery-lock write (live-pick.log), so the production-path proof rests on the test-file parity plus the isolated pick (isolated-pick.log), which reached the candidates at 42% / burn 1.7944 / pace 0.25746 but refused routing because every backend read unavailable in that isolated state.
justifications.fit: the change extends the existing _codex_rollout_candidates helper in place and adds one module constant ROLLOUT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, named by what it measures, rather than a magic literal; the new keyword parameters runs_root and live_run_ids follow the helper's existing keyword-only shape, and the sole monkeypatch of the helper (tests/test_headroom_publishes_real_readings.py:167, lambda *a, **k) stays valid. snapshot.budget_view reads the document through the same paid_lanes.read_document the preflight already uses, so no second document rule is introduced. A scan of the added lines finds no plan, sprint, ticket or author attribution. The one naming imprecision is the pre-existing stale detail string 'recorded account-window reading is stale' at snapshot.py:266, now reachable for a published reading, recorded as a follow-on and already disclosed by the node.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all three clauses of the done-when are met against reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py and reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py. The coordinator's hypothesis was tested by measurement rather than assumed: the fragment records that rollouts still land in the main home (newest main-home rate-limit event 12:15:30 UTC) and that the real cause was twofold - the installed timer invokes the publisher without a project so the 'accounts and project' guard at paid_lanes.py:929 skipped source gathering entirely, and the gatherer scanned only the main home. The fix removes the project requirement (paid_lanes.py:929, gather_sources project filter at 536-545) and scans both the main home and each run harness home (paid_lanes.py:615-631). Publication now emits codex source=rollout at 0.42 in published.json.
justifications.scope_discipline: the four commits change exactly five paths - reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py, reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, tests/test_paid_lanes_codex_window.py, tests/test_picker_dispatch_pace.py and the landing fragment - and every one is inside the manifest's declared write paths; declared-but-unused paths (reckon/budget.py, reckon/crew/window_reading.py) are correctly left untouched, no shared plan, index or sprint state is written, and the worktree is clean. The one behaviour change beyond the codex clause is the 'expired=stale' broadening at snapshot.py:261, which now lets an account-surface reading be marked expired; it is inert in practice because a fresh probe is never past the shelf life, and it is required so a stale document-sourced reading reports its age.
